claim_as_stated: Contributions from 170(b)(1)(A)(vi) organisations and governmental units are exempt from the 2% limit, so a recipient's DAF grants from (vi) sponsors stay in public support and are not in line 5.
exact_values_found: Instructions, Part II line 5: “the 2% limitation doesn’t apply to contributions from organizations qualifying as publicly supported organizations under section 170(b)(1)(A)(vi), governmental units described in section 170(b)(1)(A)(v)” and to churches, schools, hospitals etc. “only if they also qualify” under (vi). Reg. 1.170A-9(f)(6)(i): the limit does not apply to (vi) contributions “except as provided in paragraph (f)(6)(v)”; (f)(6)(v): not subject to the 2% limit “unless such contributions represent amounts which have been expressly or impliedly earmarked by a donor to such governmental unit or section 170(b)(1)(A)(vi) organization as being for, or for the benefit of, the particular organization”.
discrepancies: The quote is exact, but the study omits the regulation's earmarking (agent or conduit) exception, which the instructions do not repeat.
contradictory_evidence: The instructions say nothing specific about donor-advised funds in the line 5 text, and no instruction text treats a DAF grant as coming from the advising donor.
interpretation_challenge: Whether donor advice on a DAF grant is ‘implied earmarking’ is not settled in either text. The 98.4% (vi) share is therefore an upper bound on the DAF dollars that stay outside line 5. A filer attributing DAF grants to the donor follows a defensible reading of the regulation; it is not simply departing from the instructions, as the study's limit 3 implies.

claim_as_stated: A year with line 5850 = N has a nil DQ, so under s.149.1(21) all of its qualifying spending is a disbursement excess.
exact_values_found: DQ definition para (c): “in any other case, nil”. (21): disbursement excess is the amount by which spending on charitable activities and qualifying-disbursement gifts “exceeds its disbursement quota for the year”. Line 5850 asks whether average property exceeded C$100k (charitable organization) or C$25k (foundation).
contradictory_evidence: Line 5850 is self-reported. St. Kevin's Parish filed 5850 = N for 2023 and 2024, but its 2025 Schedule 8 line 805 is C$5,000,000 (a round figure; line 870 reads 5) and total assets were C$1.08m (FPE 2023) and C$5.70m (FPE 2024). Pemberton's 2025 line 5900 (Apr 2022–Mar 2024) is C$37,966, above its C$25k threshold, while its 2024 answer (Apr 2021–Mar 2023) was N. The parent study also found JCF Montreal with 5850 = N and C$2,143m on line 5900.
